chunks: If Umm al-Walad kills her master by mistake, then she is free and there is no liability upon her; but if she kills him intentionally, she is killed for him.
And what he narrated does not contradict these two reports:
And Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Jaʿfar, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he used to say:

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: a slave woman who has borne a child to her master
key_terms.قُتِلَتْ بِهِ: she is put to death in retaliation for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if Umm al-Walad kills her master intentionally or by mistake?
ai.summary: This text presents a legal ruling concerning Umm al-Walad if she causes the death of her master, distinguishing between accidental and intentional killing. It also introduces another report through a narrator chain, indicating comparison and reconciliation between narrations in juristic discussion.
